entities.title: CatalogItem (product entity, legacy and modernized)
entities.summary: A sellable catalog product with an id, a name (max 50), an optional description, a price (decimal, money), a picture file name (default dummy.png), required links to one brand and one type, and stock figures (available stock, restock threshold, max stock threshold) plus an on-reorder flag. In the legacy EF model it is the CatalogItems set; in the modernized model it is the Catalog table. PictureUri and TempImageName are not stored. Ids are assigned by the application (hi-lo or sequence) or by the seed, and the foreign keys cascade deletes by EF default in some versions.

claims.text: The context exposes five sets: CatalogBrands, CatalogItems, CatalogItemsStocks, CatalogTypes and DiscountItems.
CatalogItem.Id is not database generated; Price is money with precision 19,4 and Picturefilename holds the image file name.
DiscountItem has Size as double, Start and End as date columns, and Id as the key.
The brand and type names are stored as non-Unicode strings.

rules.title: Catalog item id generation with hi-lo sequences

claims.text: The hi-lo generator fetches a new block from the sequence catalog_hilo every ten ids and hands out the ids in between from memory.
When no IDs remain in the current block, the generator reads the next value of catalog_hilo and then serves nine further IDs from memory before it queries the sequence again.
The catalog_hilo, catalog_brand_hilo and catalog_type_hilo sequences each start at 1 and increment by 10.
The generator fetches a new block from the sequence catalog_hilo when no IDs remain, and then hands out the following nine IDs in memory.

rules.title: Catalog item ids come from a HiLo sequence generator

claims.text: The generator sets HiLoIncrement to 10. When no ids are left in its block, it reads NEXT VALUE FOR catalog_hilo and then uses the next nine values in memory.
The sequences catalog_hilo, catalog_brand_hilo and catalog_type_hilo are each created with START WITH 1 and INCREMENT BY 10, bigint, with the default minimum and maximum.
The generator fetches the next value of catalog_hilo only when its local block is used up; it then gives out that value and nine more in memory, before fetching again.
Each sequence (catalog_hilo, catalog_brand_hilo, catalog_type_hilo) is a bigint sequence with START WITH 1, INCREMENT BY 10, the bigint minimum and maximum, and a bare CACHE keyword with no size.

rules.title: First-run catalog database creation and seeding

claims.text: Seed runs the three sequence scripts for catalog_hilo, catalog_brand_hilo and catalog_type_hilo, then adds types, brands, items and pictures, in that order.

rules.title: Catalog service operations on catalog items

claims.text: The generator is a hi-lo id source: when its local block is empty it runs SELECT NEXT VALUE FOR catalog_hilo once, takes that value as the current id and reserves the following nine ids (HiLoIncrement of 10) to hand out without a database call.

CatalogType has an integer key and a Type name of up to 100 characters. The migrations seed five brands and four types. Key generation differs by project (identity, application-generated, or HiLo sequences).

claims.text: Column CatalogBrand.Id: int, NOT NULL, identity (SqlServer:ValueGenerationStrategy IdentityColumn), primary key (PK_CatalogBrand).
Column CatalogBrand.Brand: string with max length 100, NOT NULL.

CatalogBrand has the primary key Id, an integer generated on add with the SQL Server identity strategy, and Brand is a required string with a maximum length of 100.

rules.title: Catalog ids come from HiLo sequences

claims.text: Type ids start at the next value of catalog_type_hilo and increase by one for each type added.
Brand ids start at the next value of catalog_brand_hilo and increase by one for each brand added.
The brand seeding follows the same pattern: one NEXT VALUE FOR catalog_brand_hilo read, then each brand gets the current value and the counter goes up by one.
The sequence catalog_brand_hilo has the same definition: bigint, start 1, increment 10.

rules.title: Catalog seed data on database creation

claims.text: Types and brands take their ids from the database sequences catalog_type_hilo and catalog_brand_hilo, counting up one by one from the value returned.
Type and brand IDs start from the value read from the catalog_type_hilo or catalog_brand_hilo sequence and increase by one per row, so they do not use the item hi-lo generator.

rules.title: Database seeding and catalog pictures extraction

claims.text: Type and brand IDs are taken from the named sequences (catalog_type_hilo, catalog_brand_hilo) and incremented by one per row.

rules.title: Catalog item ids from a HiLo sequence in blocks of ten

claims.text: The generator uses a HiLo increment of 10. When its local block is empty it reads NEXT VALUE FOR catalog_hilo and then returns the following nine ids by counting up.
Catalog type and brand ids are read from the catalog_type_hilo and catalog_brand_hilo sequences when the database is seeded, and each row takes the next number.
The catalog_hilo sequence starts at 1 and increments by 10.
The generator uses a block size of 10 (HiLoIncrement). It queries NEXT VALUE FOR catalog_hilo only when no ids remain in the current block, and otherwise returns the next id in memory.

rules.title: Initial database seeding of catalog data

claims.text: Types and brands take their ids from their own sequences (catalog_type_hilo and catalog_brand_hilo), incremented by one per row. Each CSV or built-in list falls back to PreconfiguredData when the file is missing.
Seed runs the three sequence scripts (catalog_hilo, catalog_brand_hilo and catalog_type_hilo) one after another before it adds any catalog rows.
The sequence name passed for catalog types is the constant catalog_type_hilo.
catalog_brand_hilo is a bigint sequence starting at 1 and incrementing by 10, the same settings as catalog_hilo.
catalog_type_hilo is a bigint sequence starting at 1 and incrementing by 10, the same settings as catalog_hilo.

rules.title: Catalog item keys come from a hi-lo generator

claims.text: The catalog_hilo sequence starts at 1 and increments by 10, so each block is 10 keys wide.
The generator fetches the next value of the catalog_hilo sequence and hands out ten ids from it before fetching again.
The generator reads the value with SELECT NEXT VALUE FOR catalog_hilo and calls are serialised with a lock.

claims.text: The project includes three sequence scripts for the catalog hi-lo ID generators (catalog_brand_hilo, catalog_hilo and catalog_type_hilo), each copied to the output directory when newer.

entities.title: Catalog database used by the web apps
entities.summary: The MVC and WebForms containers connect to a SQL Server database named Microsoft.eShopOnContainers.Services.CatalogDb on the sql.data service.

claims.text: The MVC and WebForms containers receive a CatalogDBContext connection string pointing at server sql.data and database Microsoft.eShopOnContainers.Services.CatalogDb.
The sql.data service is a Microsoft SQL Server Windows developer image, exposed on host port 5433.

entities.title: Catalog database used by the WCF service
entities.summary: The WCF service connects to a different database name, eShopDatabase, on the same sql.data server.

claims.text: The WCF service's CatalogDBContext points to server sql.data and database eShopDatabase.
The WCF service container depends on sql.data and is published on host port 5113.

entities.title: SQL Server database instance (sql-data)
entities.summary: The manifest deploys one Windows SQL Server container, sql-data, that listens on port 1433. It is the database the application services connect to.

claims.text: The deployment runs the image microsoft/mssql-server-windows-developer on a Windows node, selected by the beta.kubernetes.io/os: windows node selector.
The Service named sql-data exposes the same database on port 1433.

entities.title: eShopDatabase SQL Server instance hosted in Kubernetes
entities.summary: The manifests deploy a Windows SQL Server container named sql-data-for-wcf, exposed on port 1433, which the WCF service connects to for the eShopDatabase database.

claims.text: A Deployment named sql-data-for-wcf runs the image microsoft/mssql-server-windows-developer on Windows nodes, with the ACCEPT_EULA variable set to Y.
A LoadBalancer Service named sql-data-for-wcf exposes port 1433 to the cluster and to outside clients.
The WCF deployment's connection string points at Server=sql-data-for-wcf and Database=eShopDatabase, so the service uses this SQL instance as its database.

entities.title: eShop WCF service hosted in Kubernetes
entities.summary: The manifests deploy the eshop/wcfservice container on Windows nodes, with one replica behind a LoadBalancer on port 80.

claims.text: A Deployment named eshop-modernized-wcf runs one replica of the image eshop/wcfservice on Windows nodes, listening on container port 80.
A rolling update strategy allows one extra pod and one unavailable pod, with minReadySeconds set to 5. The image pull policy is Always.
A LoadBalancer Service named eshop-modernized-wcf maps port 80 to container port 80.

entities.title: Application parameters
entities.summary: Application-level settings for the MVC app: instance count, Azure storage, Application Insights key, Azure AD sign-in and post-logout URI. The cloud file uses placeholders and the local files are empty.

claims.text: The manifest declares eight parameters, with defaults for instance count -1, storage and Azure AD flags False, and empty strings for the keys and IDs.

entities.title: SQL Server container service (eshopmodernized.sqldata)
entities.summary: The Service Fabric application runs a Windows SQL Server container as a stateless singleton service, reachable on TCP port 1433 under the DNS name eshopmodernized.sqldata. It is the database host that the eShop application relies on.

claims.text: The service type SQL_ContainerType runs the SQL Server image microsoft/mssql-server-windows-developer:2017 as a container host.

The application deploys the service as a stateless singleton with DNS name eshopmodernized.sqldata. Its instance count comes from the SQL_Container_InstanceCount parameter, default 1, and the Cloud.xml parameter file also sets it to 1.
The endpoint SqlData_ContainerTypeEndpoint listens on TCP port 1433 and is bound to container port 1433.

entities.title: Catalog database context
entities.summary: The catalog data is held in a CatalogDBContext Entity Framework context backed by an eShopPorted SQL Server database.

claims.text: CatalogDBContext is registered with SQL Server and the DefaultConnection string.
The default connection points at a local SQL Server LocalDB database named eShopPorted with trusted connection.
